source.title: Why LoRA Resists Label Noise: A Theoretical Framework for Noise-Robust Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies whether low-rank LoRA capacity affects memorization of corrupted labels and reports training outcomes and training dynamics. This conceptually bears on V1's coexistence of memorization capacity and generalization, but it does not test the natural-label versus fixed-random-label setup in V1.
record.gate_note: Reports LoRA training accuracy across injected noise rates and ranks, and clean/noisy sample loss during training. These are the study's own results. Classification accuracy comparisons in Table 1 concern noisy-label training methods and do not establish the claim's held-out natural-label generalization result. RACT detection metrics and its method comparisons are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures rank-dependent fitting of partially corrupted labels and clean/noisy training-loss dynamics in LoRA fine-tuning. It does not test V1's coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization under the same recipe. Its other experiments evaluate noise detection and noisy-label training methods, without testing V2–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but abbreviated. The authors argue that low rank constrains arbitrary-label fitting, derive an optimal-rank tradeoff, and describe temporal separation between clean learning and noise memorization. They use these ideas for RACT noise detection, reporting competitive classification accuracy in their PEFT setting. Their capacity bound is existential, and their experiments do not establish V1's held-out clean-versus-random-label comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Uses low-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning on pretrained backbones and synthetic symmetric label noise; the claim versions concern random-label memorization and held-out generalization under standard training. Experiments use AdamW and compare noisy-label methods, not the claim's original setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Rank and injected noise rate change whether training accuracy reaches 100%; larger rank reduces the clean-to-noisy learning delay. Dataset and task type also vary in reported detection and classification results, outside the versions' measured outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: On AG News, all tested LoRA ranks exceed 99% training accuracy without injected noise; ranks 2 and 4 fail to fit all corrupted labels, whereas ranks 32 and 64 approach perfect training accuracy even at 40% corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA adapter rank affects the capacity to fit partially corrupted training labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean-sample training loss falls before corrupted-sample loss; larger ranks shorten the delay before noise memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA fine-tuning learns clean patterns before memorizing injected label noise, with timing dependent on rank.

record.problems: The paper states experiments focus on medium-scale benchmarks and use symmetric label noise; the capacity bound is existential and asymptotic, and the theory relies on simplifying assumptions including a linearized regime and squared loss for the exact decomposition. The AG News rank sweep is single-seed. No held-out natural-label versus random-label generalization test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Table 1's noisy-label classification accuracy and Tables 2–6's RACT detection, rank-gap, and threshold results measure noisy-label method performance or detection rather than the outcomes named by these claim versions.

untested.parts: The joint comparison of near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting, above-chance natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; changing adapter rank does not test this.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error; dropout is configured but not experimentally compared.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Neither failure to memorize corrupted labels at low rank nor successful fitting at high rank alone supports or challenges V1. The omitted method-performance tables were explicitly declared in rows_left_out and do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fixed random labels against natural labels, report held-out test accuracy against chance for random labels, or test the specified architectures and recipes.

rows.subject: LoRA adapters, ranks r ∈ {2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}
rows.operation_detail: Varied LoRA rank and injected symmetric label-noise rate; measured final training accuracy after convergence (50 epochs, early stopping disabled).
rows.value: At 0% noise, all ranks achieve near-perfect training accuracy (> 99%); at higher noise rates, ranks 2 and 4 are capped below 100%, while ranks 32 and 64 can approach 100% even at 40% noise.
rows.note: These are training accuracy results on synthetically corrupted labels, not held-out generalization results; the paper's observations state the qualitative outcomes but give no exact accuracies by rank.
rows.check: Training accuracy under partial label corruption cannot establish V1's joint memorization/generalization result. The reported qualitative values match Appendix A.2, but this row bundles ranks and noise conditions; it provides neither a fully random-label comparison nor held-out accuracy for clean and random labels.

rows.subject: LoRA (r=8)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked loss on clean and corrupted-label samples and rank-discrepancy noise-detection F1 during training.

conditions.value: not stated in text for this setup

rows.measure: Training loss on clean versus noisy samples over epochs
rows.value: Clean-sample loss decreases rapidly in early epochs; noisy-sample loss initially plateaus, then decreases as the model begins memorizing noise.
rows.note: Temporal ordering is reported, but this measures training loss under injected label noise, not natural-label held-out test error.
rows.check: The clean/noisy training-loss sequence matches Appendix B.2, but measures learning dynamics rather than V1's coexistence result. Noise-detection F1, mentioned in the operation, is a separate measure outside these versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
